chunks: With this chain, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever recites 'Qul Awha ilayya' frequently will not be affected in his worldly life by anything from the eyes of the Jinn, nor their breath, nor their sorcery, nor their machinations, and he will be with Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).
And he will say: 'O Lord, I do not desire any substitute for it, nor do I desire to turn away from it.'

key_terms.أَعْيُنِ الْجِنِّ: Ayn al-Jinn (The evil eye of the Jinn)
key_terms.قُلْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ: Qul Awha ilayya (Say, it was revealed to me) - Refers to Surah Al-Jinn
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٍ ص: Muhammad SAWW (The Prophet Muhammad and his family)
key_terms.نَفْثِهِمْ: Nafthihim (Their breath/spit - a form of Jinn influence)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits of reciting Surah Jinn according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith emphasizes the protective efficacy of frequently reciting Surah Al-Jinn, specifically invoking the divine revelation aspect ('Qul Awha ilayya') to ward off Jinn's evil eye, breath, sorcery, and schemes. It further promises spiritual companionship with the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), grounded in the supplication 'Ya Rabb la uridu bihi badalan' (O Lord, I do not desire any substitute for it), reflecting the Shia tradition of linking Quranic recitation with tangible worldly protection and otherworldly proximity to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from Hanan b. Sadeer from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

Whoever recites it often would neither be affected by the evil eye of Jinn in his worldly life, nor can there be any effect on him of sorcery, now can any harm occur to him through any kind of machination or Satanic action of the Jinn. Also the reciter of Surah Jinn would be in the company of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) and his Progeny (a.s.).
